Ui.Script:
BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON = "Interface\\Icons\\INV_Misc_QuestionMark"
-- Ref ActionButton.lua:4 / UIParent.lua: the flash blink period and the range-check cadence. ATTACK_BUTTON_FLASH_TIME = 0.4 TOOLTIP_UPDATE_TIME = 0.2
-- CooldownFrame_SetTimer moved to Cooldown.xml (the ref's own file split) — the bag -- slots share it, so it loads before both consumers.
-- One button's HotKey corner — the ref's ActionButton_UpdateHotkeys law in FULL since -- 1008 (closing 0997's raw-token residue): the ABBREVIATED binding text through the -- real GetBindingText transcription (UIParent.xml — one modifier abbreviates, "s-2"; -- two or more collapse to the ref's "·"), and with NO binding the ref's no-binding -- leg — an empty label the OnUpdate range timer fills with the RANGE_INDICATOR dot -- while out of range (until 1008 that leg was multibar-only; now any unbound slot, -- main bar included, wears it). A harness with no registered bindings paints nothing. function BenillaActionButton_PaintHotkey(button) local key = GetBindingKey(button.bindingCommand) local text if GetBindingText then text = GetBindingText(key, "KEY_", 1) else -- lone-file harness (the shipped manifest always has UIParent.xml first): -- the raw token, the MicroMenu.xml fallback idiom. text = key or "" end button.noBindingLabel = (text == "") button.hotkey:SetText(text) end
-- Every button's label, repainted on UPDATE_BINDINGS (a rebind, a set switch, the seed). function BenillaActionBar_UpdateHotkeys() for i = 1, table.getn(BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS) do BenillaActionButton_PaintHotkey(BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS[i]) end end
-- Whether a placeable cursor payload is held (decision 0216 §7's ACTIONBAR_SHOWGRID/ -- _HIDEGRID pair, simplified to a boolean — see the SCOPE note above). BENILLA_ACTIONBAR_GRID_SHOWN = false
-- Every live action button — the main bar's 12 plus the multibars' (MultiBars.xml joins -- at OnLoad). The fan-out roster for the bar-level events below: the ref registers the -- feedback events per-button; our bar-level fan needs the full set in one place. BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS = {}
-- Seat a TOP-LEVEL frame that anchors INTO the bar art (the bag bar + backpack toggle, -- BagFrame.xml; the micro-button row, MicroMenu.xml) one frame level above the art, so its -- icons draw over the bar plate instead of under it. -- -- Why it's needed: those frames are top-level, so they default to a LOWER frame level than -- the bar's own art (a child hierarchy — the ExpBar's dwarf notches + the metal/well art sit -- at the bar's child level). Frame level dominates the flat painter's order, so the bar art -- would paint OVER them — the ring shows but the centered icon is fully covered (the "empty -- rings, no bag icons" bug). The bar's OWN 12 buttons avoid this by being CHILDREN of the art -- frame (child-over-parent). (SetParent onto the art frame would be the structural twin, but -- the engine keys draw order at creation and does not re-key on a runtime reparent, so the -- explicit level is the reliable lever.) Lives here, with the frame it's about, because two -- files now need it — it began as BagFrame.xml's private BenillaBagBar_SeatAboveActionBar. function BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove(frame) local art = getglobal("BenillaActionBarArtFrame") if art then frame:SetFrameLevel(art:GetFrameLevel() + 1) end end
-- ── The keyring's half of the bar (ref MainMenuBar_UpdateKeyRing, MainMenuBar.lua -- l.174-183; decision 0765) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- The keyring is not just a button bolted onto the bar: the bar's two RIGHT-hand strips are -- re-textured to a variant plate that has a socket for it, and the performance meter slides -- 8px further left out of the way. Both atlases are 256-wide 43px strips at the same on- -- screen size and anchors, so only the file + TexCoords change (UI-MainMenuBar-KeyRing is -- 256x128 and holds exactly the two bands the ref names: 0.3359375 * 128 = 43px each). -- -- Called by BenillaKeyRingButton's own OnEvent (BagFrame.xml). Everything is nil-guarded: -- this file loads without BagFrame.xml in several harnesses, and BagFrame.xml loads without -- this one in ~25 bag/bank/escape/merchant tests — either way the missing half no-ops. -- -- DIVERGENCE (decision 0765): the ref latches this ON forever the first time HasKey() is -- true, via the saved variable SHOW_KEYRING (and pulses the button for 60s to announce it). -- This engine has no saved variables, and a session-scoped latch would leak across a -- character switch — showing a keyring on a character with no key — so the state is derived -- from HasKey() on every BAG_UPDATE instead, in BOTH directions. Observably identical -- unless you destroy your last key, which then un-shows the keyring rather than leaving an -- empty one behind. The 60s pulse is out, consistently with decision 0304's "no button -- pulse" for the micro buttons. function BenillaMainMenuBar_UpdateKeyRing() local show = HasKey and HasKey() -- The two right-hand strips (BenillaActionBarTexture2 at x=+128, Texture3 at x=+384), -- keyring plate or the ordinary dwarf plate. The dwarf coords are this file's own -- authored ones (see the strips below) — restated here because this is the only code -- that ever changes them back. local strips = { { name = "BenillaActionBarTexture2", keyring = 0.6640625, keyringBottom = 1.0, dwarf = 0.33203125, dwarfBottom = 0.5 }, { name = "BenillaActionBarTexture3", keyring = 0.1640625, keyringBottom = 0.5, dwarf = 0.08203125, dwarfBottom = 0.25 }, } for _, strip in ipairs(strips) do local tex = getglobal(strip.name) if tex then if show then tex:SetTexture("Interface\\MainMenuBar\\UI-MainMenuBar-KeyRing") tex:SetTexCoord(0, 1, strip.keyring, strip.keyringBottom) else tex:SetTexture("Interface\\MainMenuBar\\UI-MainMenuBar-Dwarf") tex:SetTexCoord(0, 1, strip.dwarf, strip.dwarfBottom) end end end -- The performance meter's recess moves with the plate: -227 without the keyring, -- -235 with it (ref l.180). Its own comment at the foot of this file has the geometry. local perf = getglobal("BenillaPerformanceBarFrame") local bar = getglobal("BenillaActionBar") if perf and bar then perf:SetPoint("BOTTOMRIGHT", bar, "BOTTOMRIGHT", (show and -235) or -227, -10) end local button = getglobal("BenillaKeyRingButton") if button then if show then button:Show() else button:Hide() end end -- Losing the last key with the keyring open would strand an orphan window; the ref -- can't reach this state (its latch is one-way), so this is ours to decide. local frame = getglobal("BenillaKeyRingFrame") if frame and not show and frame:IsShown() then frame:Hide() end end
-- The wire/API action id the MAIN bar's button i displays (the vanilla page formula). -- INTERNAL to BenillaActionButton_Action below — the ONLY caller. A button path that -- reaches past it computes a MAIN-bar id for a multibar button (base ignored), which -- reads as "the slot below": the tooltip hover did exactly that until 2026-07-21. function BenillaActionBar_ActionFor(index) local offset = GetBonusBarOffset() local base = 0 if offset > 0 then base = (6 + offset - 1) * 12 end return base + index end
-- The action id a specific BUTTON displays: the ref forks on the parent frame's NAME -- (ActionButton_GetPagedID:446-467 — MultiBarBottomLeft ⇒ page 6, MultiBarBottomRight ⇒ -- page 5, else the paged/bonus formula); we carry the fork as data — a fixed per-button -- page base set at OnLoad (MultiBars.xml), nil for the bonus-paged main bar. function BenillaActionButton_Action(button) if button.base then return button.base + button.index end return BenillaActionBar_ActionFor(button.index) end
-- Hover: SetAction's pure delegation (decision 0276 — a SPELL slot renders the spell -- tooltip with its rank column, an ITEM slot the shared item renderer; ref -- ActionButton_SetTooltip). The re-enter keeps it live across page flips. -- Anchor: ref ActionButton_SetTooltip (ActionButton.lua l.366-372) branches on the -- UberTooltips CVar — "1" → the default corner, else RIGHT/LEFT by bar. UberTooltips -- registers with default "1" (byte-read: WoW.exe 0x48fdd9, default string 0x82e748; -- sibling rows BlockTrades→"0", UnitNameRenderMode→"2" confirm the layout), and benilla -- ships no CVar state, so the branch collapses to the stock-client one: action-bar -- tooltips live at the screen's bottom-right, above the bags. function BenillaActionButton_OnEnter(button) if not GameTooltip then return end -- engine tests load file subsets GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, button) GameTooltip:SetAction(BenillaActionButton_Action(button)) end
function BenillaActionButton_OnLoad(button, index, base, commandPrefix) button.index = index button.base = base button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon") button.hotkey = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "HotKey") button.count = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count") button.flash = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Flash") button.border = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Border") button.cooldown = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Cooldown") -- Ref ActionButton_OnLoad:104-106: the flash/range state the OnUpdate loop drives. button.flashing = 0 button.flashtime = 0 button.rangeTimer = nil -- Every bar button carries its binding COMMAND (0997 main bar, 1008 multibars): -- the caller names the command family (MultiBars.xml passes MULTIACTIONBAR1/2BUTTON -- — the ref's own bar↔page mapping quoted there); nothing passed = the main bar's -- ACTIONBUTTON. The label paints from it here and repaints on UPDATE_BINDINGS. button.bindingCommand = (commandPrefix or "ACTIONBUTTON") .. index BenillaActionButton_PaintHotkey(button) table.insert(BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS, button) -- BOTH mouse buttons, ref-verbatim (ActionButton_OnLoad, ActionButton.lua:108-109): -- an action button is a two-button button. The OnClick body reads no `arg1` — in the -- ref either button runs the same PickupAction/UseAction fork — so right-click USES -- the action, which is how food and spells are used off the bar. Without this the -- widget default ({"LeftButtonUp"}, `benilla_ui::script::button`) silently swallowed -- every right-click on the bar (director's report B200). button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") -- The drag trio (decision 0216 §3/§7): click-carry and drag share one downstream path -- by construction (OnClick/OnDragStart both call PickupAction; OnReceiveDrag calls -- PlaceAction — ref ActionBarFrame.xml:12-38). Both buttons drag, ref-verbatim too -- (l.108) — a started drag suppresses the click, so right-press-and-move relocates the -- action while right-click-in-place still uses it. LOCK_ACTIONBAR stays the vanilla -- default (unlocked), so unlike the ref's cvar guard, drag is always live here. button:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton", "RightButton") BenillaActionButton_Update(button) end
-- Ref ActionBarFrame.xml:12-22's fork verbatim: shift picks up, else uses (checkCursor=1 — -- the engine routes a click-with-payload to PlaceAction instead, decision 0216 §7). function BenillaActionButton_OnClick(button) local action = BenillaActionButton_Action(button) if IsShiftKeyDown() then PickupAction(action) else UseAction(action, 1) end BenillaActionButton_Update(button) end
function BenillaActionButton_OnDragStart(button) PickupAction(BenillaActionButton_Action(button)) BenillaActionButton_Update(button) end
function BenillaActionButton_OnReceiveDrag(button) PlaceAction(BenillaActionButton_Action(button)) BenillaActionButton_Update(button) end
-- The default ACTIONBUTTON1..12 key bindings (ref Bindings.xml:121-127: keys 1..9,0,-,= -- run ActionButtonDown on keystate "down" and ActionButtonUp on "up" via runOnUp), both -- transcribed from ActionButton.lua:15-28/30-45 and routed here from the app's key feed. -- DOWN pushes the button only from NORMAL; UP fires the action only from PUSHED — the -- state pair is both the pushed visual and the debounce (a key-repeat DOWN or a stray UP -- is a no-op). Calls UseAction DIRECTLY with NO checkCursor argument — unlike the -- mouse-click fork above, a keybind never places (decision 0216 §7: the ref itself never -- routes ActionButtonUp through OnClick, so this no longer goes through Click() either — -- the two entry points share the id formula, not the click path). The ref's -- BonusActionBar fork and the SELFACTIONBUTTON onSelf argument are not modeled (no bonus -- bar frame, no self-cast modifier binding). function BenillaActionButtonDown(index) local button = getglobal("BenillaActionButton" .. index) if ( button:GetButtonState() == "NORMAL" ) then button:SetButtonState("PUSHED") end end
function BenillaActionButtonUp(index) local button = getglobal("BenillaActionButton" .. index) if ( button:GetButtonState() == "PUSHED" ) then button:SetButtonState("NORMAL") UseAction(BenillaActionButton_Action(button)) -- Ref ActionButtonUp:55-59: the checked ring reflects the use immediately. BenillaActionButton_UpdateState(button) end end
-- Ref ActionButton_UpdateState:261-267 — the checked ring: the current action (Attack -- while auto-attacking, the in-flight cast) or the live auto-repeat spell. function BenillaActionButton_UpdateState(button) local action = BenillaActionButton_Action(button) if ( IsCurrentAction(action) or IsAutoRepeatAction(action) ) then button:SetChecked(1) else button:SetChecked(0) end end
-- Ref ActionButton_UpdateUsable:269-283, verbatim colors: usable white; out of power the -- blue-grey 0.5/0.5/1.0 on icon AND ring; otherwise-unusable the 0.4 grey icon only. function BenillaActionButton_UpdateUsable(button) local action = BenillaActionButton_Action(button) local normalTexture = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "NormalTexture") local isUsable, notEnoughMana = IsUsableAction(action) if ( isUsable ) then button.icon:SetVertexColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) normalTexture:SetVertexColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) elseif ( notEnoughMana ) then button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.5, 0.5, 1.0) normalTexture:SetVertexColor(0.5, 0.5, 1.0) else button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.4, 0.4, 0.4) normalTexture:SetVertexColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) end end
-- Ref ActionButton_UpdateCooldown:294-298. function BenillaActionButton_UpdateCooldown(button) local start, duration, enable = GetActionCooldown(BenillaActionButton_Action(button)) CooldownFrame_SetTimer(button.cooldown, start, duration, enable) end
-- Ref ActionButton_UpdateFlash/StartFlash/StopFlash/IsFlashing:469-496: the red blink on -- an engaged Attack button / a live auto-repeat, toggled by the OnUpdate loop below. function BenillaActionButton_UpdateFlash(button) local action = BenillaActionButton_Action(button) if ( (IsAttackAction(action) and IsCurrentAction(action)) or IsAutoRepeatAction(action) ) then BenillaActionButton_StartFlash(button) else BenillaActionButton_StopFlash(button) end end
function BenillaActionButton_StartFlash(button) button.flashing = 1 button.flashtime = 0 BenillaActionButton_UpdateState(button) end
function BenillaActionButton_StopFlash(button) button.flashing = 0 button.flash:Hide() BenillaActionButton_UpdateState(button) end
-- Ref ActionButton_OnUpdate:384-428, minus the tooltip refresh (no per-button tooltip -- yet): the 0.4 s flash toggle, and the 0.2 s range recheck — a bound slot's label -- tints red/grey, an unbound one wears the RANGE_INDICATOR dot (both legs the ref's, -- unified in 1008 — the SCOPE note). function BenillaActionButton_OnUpdate(button, elapsed) if ( button.flashing == 1 ) then button.flashtime = button.flashtime - elapsed if ( button.flashtime <= 0 ) then local overtime = -button.flashtime if ( overtime >= ATTACK_BUTTON_FLASH_TIME ) then overtime = 0 end button.flashtime = ATTACK_BUTTON_FLASH_TIME - overtime if ( button.flash:IsVisible() ) then button.flash:Hide() else button.flash:Show() end end end if ( button.rangeTimer ) then button.rangeTimer = button.rangeTimer - elapsed if ( button.rangeTimer <= 0 ) then if ( IsActionInRange(BenillaActionButton_Action(button)) == 0 ) then -- An UNBOUND button has no label to tint: paint the ref's -- RANGE_INDICATOR dot instead (net ref behavior — red dot iff out of -- range). Since 1008 the fork is the binding text itself (any bar's -- slot can be bound or bare now), not which bar owns the button. if button.noBindingLabel then button.hotkey:SetText("●") end button.hotkey:SetVertexColor(1.0, 0.1, 0.1) else if button.noBindingLabel then button.hotkey:SetText("") end button.hotkey:SetVertexColor(0.6, 0.6, 0.6) end button.rangeTimer = TOOLTIP_UPDATE_TIME end end end
-- ref ActionButton.lua:285-292 ActionButton_UpdateCount, transcribed. The gate is -- IsConsumableAction, NOT "count > 0": a consumable you have run out of shows a literal -- "0", and an item that is not consumable (a mount, a trinket, a bag) shows nothing at -- all, however many copies you hold. function BenillaActionButton_UpdateCount(button) local action = BenillaActionButton_Action(button) if IsConsumableAction(action) then button.count:SetText(GetActionCount(action)) else button.count:SetText("") end end
function BenillaActionButton_Update(button) local action = BenillaActionButton_Action(button) if HasAction(action) then button.icon:SetTexture(GetActionTexture(action) or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON) button.icon:Show() button:SetNormalTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-Quickslot2") button:Show() button.rangeTimer = -1 BenillaActionButton_UpdateCount(button) BenillaActionButton_UpdateState(button) BenillaActionButton_UpdateUsable(button) BenillaActionButton_UpdateCooldown(button) BenillaActionButton_UpdateFlash(button) else -- ref l.168: the empty arm HIDES the icon region — it does not clear the path. The -- distinction is load-bearing here: UpdateUsable's SetVertexColor tint survives a -- SetTexture(nil) ("a tint outlives the art"), and an occupied slot going empty on -- a character switch left that white tint on a pathless region — the solid white -- buttons of the 2026-08-07 report (decision 1108, with the engine-side draw gate). button.icon:Hide() button.count:SetText("") button.cooldown:Hide() button.rangeTimer = nil button.hotkey:SetVertexColor(0.6, 0.6, 0.6) button:SetChecked(0) BenillaActionButton_StopFlash(button) if button.base then -- An EMPTY multibar well is the ref's own default: hidden entirely, appearing -- as a drop-target ring only while a payload is held (ActionButton_Update's -- showgrid==0 Hide; MultiActionBar_ShowAllGrids). Only the MAIN bar keeps our -- always-visible wells divergence (the SCOPE note) — its art has sockets; -- floating rings over bare world would not read as a bar. button.hotkey:SetText("") if BENILLA_ACTIONBAR_GRID_SHOWN then button:SetNormalTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-Quickslot") button:Show() else button:Hide() end else -- While a payload is held, an empty slot shows the ref's own "no action" ring -- (Interface\Buttons\UI-Quickslot) so it reads as a drop target; otherwise the -- plain occupied-style ring, unchanged from before this slice (SCOPE note). if BENILLA_ACTIONBAR_GRID_SHOWN then button:SetNormalTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-Quickslot") else button:SetNormalTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-Quickslot2") end end end -- Ref ActionButton_Update:221-228: the equipped-item green border. if ( IsEquippedAction(action) ) then button.border:SetVertexColor(0, 1.0, 0, 0.35) button.border:Show() else button.border:Hide() end end
function BenillaActionBar_OnLoad(frame) frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") frame:RegisterEvent("ACTIONBAR_SLOT_CHANGED") frame:RegisterEvent("UPDATE_BONUS_ACTIONBAR") frame:RegisterEvent("ACTIONBAR_SHOWGRID") frame:RegisterEvent("ACTIONBAR_HIDEGRID") -- The state/feedback events (ref ActionButton_OnLoad's per-button set, registered -- bar-level here — the SCOPE note): the app fires each on the byte-mapped client -- edge (wow-re action-button-state-api.md). frame:RegisterEvent("ACTIONBAR_UPDATE_STATE") frame:RegisterEvent("ACTIONBAR_UPDATE_USABLE") frame:RegisterEvent("ACTIONBAR_UPDATE_COOLDOWN") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_AURAS_CHANGED") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTER_COMBAT") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_LEAVE_COMBAT") frame:RegisterEvent("START_AUTOREPEAT_SPELL") frame:RegisterEvent("STOP_AUTOREPEAT_SPELL") -- The binding table moved (a rebind, a set switch, the seed) — repaint the HotKey -- corners (0997; the ref's own UPDATE_BINDINGS consumer is UpdateHotkeys too). frame:RegisterEvent("UPDATE_BINDINGS") end
-- Run one ref per-button handler over the OCCUPIED buttons (the bar-level fan — SCOPE -- note). The HasAction gate is the ref's own semantics, load-bearing, not an optimization: -- ActionButton.lua registers these handlers only while the button has an action ("All -- event handlers below this line are only set when the button has an action"), so an -- empty button never runs them — UpdateUsable on an empty would land its 0.4 grey -- SetVertexColor on the texture-less icon region, which draws as a solid grey plate -- (the director's empty-wells report, 2026-07-10). function BenillaActionBar_ForEach(fn) for i = 1, table.getn(BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS) do local button = BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS[i] if HasAction(BenillaActionButton_Action(button)) then fn(button) end end end
function BenillaActionBar_OnEvent(frame) -- ACTIONBAR_SLOT_CHANGED names its action in arg1; repaint just the button showing it. if event == "ACTIONBAR_SLOT_CHANGED" and arg1 then for i = 1, table.getn(BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS) do local button = BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS[i] if BenillaActionButton_Action(button) == arg1 then BenillaActionButton_Update(button) end end return end if event == "UPDATE_BINDINGS" then BenillaActionBar_UpdateHotkeys() return end -- The ref ActionButton_OnEvent dispatch (l.332-362), fanned bar-level: if event == "ACTIONBAR_UPDATE_STATE" then BenillaActionBar_ForEach(BenillaActionButton_UpdateState) return end if event == "ACTIONBAR_UPDATE_USABLE" or event == "ACTIONBAR_UPDATE_COOLDOWN" then BenillaActionBar_ForEach(BenillaActionButton_UpdateUsable) BenillaActionBar_ForEach(BenillaActionButton_UpdateCooldown) return end if event == "PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED" or event == "PLAYER_AURAS_CHANGED" then BenillaActionBar_ForEach(BenillaActionButton_UpdateUsable) return end if event == "PLAYER_ENTER_COMBAT" then BenillaActionBar_ForEach(function(b) if IsAttackAction(BenillaActionButton_Action(b)) then BenillaActionButton_StartFlash(b) end end) return end if event == "PLAYER_LEAVE_COMBAT" then BenillaActionBar_ForEach(function(b) if IsAttackAction(BenillaActionButton_Action(b)) then BenillaActionButton_StopFlash(b) end end) return end if event == "START_AUTOREPEAT_SPELL" then BenillaActionBar_ForEach(function(b) if IsAutoRepeatAction(BenillaActionButton_Action(b)) then BenillaActionButton_StartFlash(b) end end) return end if event == "STOP_AUTOREPEAT_SPELL" then BenillaActionBar_ForEach(function(b) if b.flashing == 1 and not IsAttackAction(BenillaActionButton_Action(b)) then BenillaActionButton_StopFlash(b) end end) return end if event == "ACTIONBAR_SHOWGRID" or event == "ACTIONBAR_HIDEGRID" then BENILLA_ACTIONBAR_GRID_SHOWN = (event == "ACTIONBAR_SHOWGRID") end for i = 1, table.getn(BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS) do BenillaActionButton_Update(BENILLA_ACTION_BUTTONS[i]) end end
-- The XP bar (ref-MainMenuBar.lua MainMenuExpBar_Update): value = current XP within the -- level, max = XP-to-level. Both from the player-global UnitXP feed (PLAYER_XP / -- PLAYER_NEXT_LEVEL_XP). currXP >= 0 so min(0,currXP) is just 0. function BenillaExpBar_Update(bar) local currXP = UnitXP("player") local nextXP = UnitXPMax("player") bar:SetMinMaxValues(0, nextXP) bar:SetValue(currXP) end
function BenillaExpBar_OnLoad(bar) bar:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") bar:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_XP_UPDATE") -- The numerals seam (ref-MainMenuBar.xml l.117-120: TextStatusBar_Initialize() + -- textLockable in the bar's own OnLoad; TextStatusBar.xml). textLockable is what lets -- the statusBarText cvar pin the numerals on permanently. if TextStatusBar_Initialize then -- engine tests load file subsets TextStatusBar_Initialize() bar.textLockable = 1 end BenillaExpBar_Update(bar) end
-- ref-MainMenuBar.xml l.121-126: repaint, then hand arg1/arg2 to the CVAR_UPDATE watcher. function BenillaExpBar_OnEvent(bar) BenillaExpBar_Update(bar) if TextStatusBar_OnEvent then TextStatusBar_OnEvent(arg1, arg2) end end
-- The XP bar's hover (ref-MainMenuBar.xml l.136-147, MainMenuExpBar's own OnEnter/OnLeave). -- ref GlobalStrings.lua l.5461 / l.2789 / l.1929-1932 (enUS), in the `X = X or` FALLBACK -- form: the app runs the real localized GlobalStrings.lua off the patch chain BEFORE this -- file (ui_script/mod.rs load_global_strings), so the installed locale wins and these -- copies only fill in for the test harnesses, which load no patch chain. -- CombatText.xml's shape. XPBAR_LABEL = XPBAR_LABEL or "XP Bar" NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_XPBAR = NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_XPBAR or "The amount of experience (XP) you have earned. The color of the XP bar indicates your rest state: light blue for Rested, and purple for Normal. Rested players earn twice the experience they would normally gain from slaying a monster. Characters become less rested when they kill monsters, and more rested by spending time at or logging out at an inn or city." EXHAUST_TOOLTIP1 = EXHAUST_TOOLTIP1 or "|cffffd200%s|r\n|cffffffff%d%% of normal experience\ngained from monsters.|r" EXHAUST_TOOLTIP2 = EXHAUST_TOOLTIP2 or "\n|cffff0000You should rest at an Inn.|r" EXHAUST_TOOLTIP4 = EXHAUST_TOOLTIP4 or "\n\n|cffffd200Resting|r\n|cffffffffYou must rest for %d additional\nminutes to become|r |cffffd200Fully Rested|r|cffffffff.|r"
-- The ref OnEnter's full body (ref-MainMenuBar.xml l.136-141), now that its machinery -- exists (decision 1082): the on-bar numerals (TextStatusBar.xml), the 1 s armed timer -- that appends the rest-state line to the held-open tooltip, and canAddRestStateLine — -- the handshake BenillaExhaustionToolTipText's newbie-tips branch reads. The trailing 1 -- is the ref's noNormalText: with detailed tips OFF this hover shows NOTHING rather than -- a bare "XP Bar". Transcribed, though 1.12's default (0661) never takes it. function BenillaExpBar_OnEnter(bar) if TextStatusBar_UpdateTextString then -- engine tests load file subsets TextStatusBar_UpdateTextString(bar) ShowTextStatusBarText(bar) end BenillaExhaustionTick.timer = 1 if not GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip then return end GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip(bar, XPBAR_LABEL, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_XPBAR, 1) GameTooltip.canAddRestStateLine = 1 end
function BenillaExpBar_OnLeave(bar) if HideTextStatusBarText then HideTextStatusBarText(bar) end if GameTooltip then GameTooltip:Hide() end BenillaExhaustionTick.timer = nil end
-- ── The max-level rail (ref-ReputationFrame.lua, the max-level slice) ───────────────── -- ref l.14: the constant lives in ReputationFrame.lua, which isn't built yet — it moves -- there with the reputation system. MAX_PLAYER_LEVEL = 60
function BenillaMaxLevelBar_OnLoad(bar) bar:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") bar:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_LEVEL_UP") end
-- ref ReputationWatchBar_Update's else arm (ref-ReputationFrame.lua l.161-166 + -- l.236-244), the no-watched-faction branch only — the reputation branches wait for the -- reputation system: at MAX_PLAYER_LEVEL the XP strip gives way to the rail and the -- tick goes with it. Login seam: the ref initializes off UPDATE_FACTION (its OnEvent's -- else arm; the faction list lands at every login), an event benilla doesn't carry yet, -- so the rail listens to PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD instead — same moment, same values. function BenillaMaxLevelBar_Update(newLevel) if not newLevel then newLevel = UnitLevel("player") end if newLevel == MAX_PLAYER_LEVEL then BenillaExpBar:Hide() BenillaMaxLevelBar:Show() BenillaExhaustionTick:Hide() else BenillaExpBar:Show() BenillaMaxLevelBar:Hide() end end
-- The ref's event fan (ref-ReputationFrame.xml l.1002-1016): PLAYER_LEVEL_UP passes -- arg1 (the new level — the level FIELD may not have landed yet), everything else -- re-reads UnitLevel. function BenillaMaxLevelBar_OnEvent() if event == "PLAYER_LEVEL_UP" then BenillaMaxLevelBar_Update(arg1) else BenillaMaxLevelBar_Update() end end
-- ── The exhaustion tick (ref-MainMenuBar.lua ExhaustionTick_*) ──────────────────────── -- The round marker riding the XP bar at the point where rested XP runs out, plus the -- pale fill between the bar's value and that point. One transcription cut left, named: -- the ref's two ReputationWatchBar guards (the max-level+rep tick hide, l.51-54, and -- the rep-bar-replaced-the-xp-bar hide, l.69-71) reference the faction watch bar, not -- built — its frame can't be shown, so the cut is an unreachable-code cut, not a -- behavior cut. The MainMenuBarMaxLevelBar guard is live since 1094 (the rail below). function BenillaExhaustionTick_OnLoad(tick) tick:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") tick:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_XP_UPDATE") tick:RegisterEvent("UPDATE_EXHAUSTION") tick:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_LEVEL_UP") tick:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_UPDATE_RESTING") end
function BenillaExhaustionTick_Update(tick) if event == "PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD" or event == "PLAYER_XP_UPDATE" or event == "UPDATE_EXHAUSTION" or event == "PLAYER_LEVEL_UP" then local playerCurrXP = UnitXP("player") local playerMaxXP = UnitXPMax("player") local exhaustionThreshold = GetXPExhaustion() local exhaustionStateID = GetRestState() -- The ref's beta-eras leftover: the tired/exhausted tiers (id >= 3) park the tick -- at the bar's RIGHT end. The live server never produces them (GetRestState's -- binding note) — kept because the ref keeps it. if exhaustionStateID >= 3 then tick:SetPoint("CENTER", "BenillaExpBar", "RIGHT", 0, 0) end if not exhaustionThreshold then tick:Hide() BenillaExhaustionLevelFillBar:Hide() else local exhaustionTickSet = max(((playerCurrXP + exhaustionThreshold) / playerMaxXP) * BenillaExpBar:GetWidth(), 0) tick:ClearAllPoints() if exhaustionTickSet > BenillaExpBar:GetWidth() or BenillaMaxLevelBar:IsShown() then tick:Hide() BenillaExhaustionLevelFillBar:Hide() else tick:Show() tick:SetPoint("CENTER", "BenillaExpBar", "LEFT", exhaustionTickSet, 0) BenillaExhaustionLevelFillBar:Show() BenillaExhaustionLevelFillBar:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", "BenillaExpBar", "TOPLEFT", exhaustionTickSet, 0) end end end -- The rest-state paint (only these two events repaint it, the ref's own split): -- rested = light blue bar + pale blue fill-to-tick, normal = the purple default. if event == "PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD" or event == "UPDATE_EXHAUSTION" then local exhaustionStateID = GetRestState() if exhaustionStateID == 1 then BenillaExpBar:SetStatusBarColor(0.0, 0.39, 0.88, 1.0) BenillaExhaustionLevelFillBar:SetVertexColor(0.0, 0.39, 0.88, 0.15) BenillaExhaustionTickHighlight:SetVertexColor(0.0, 0.39, 0.88) elseif exhaustionStateID == 2 then BenillaExpBar:SetStatusBarColor(0.58, 0.0, 0.55, 1.0) BenillaExhaustionLevelFillBar:SetVertexColor(0.58, 0.0, 0.55, 0.15) BenillaExhaustionTickHighlight:SetVertexColor(0.58, 0.0, 0.55) end end end
-- The tick's tooltip (ref-MainMenuBar.lua ExhaustionToolTipText, the live branches only — -- its own dead commented-out code is not carried). Two callers, two postures: hovering -- the TICK anchors the plate beside it (flipped to whichever side has room); the armed -- 1 s timer from the BAR hover instead APPENDS the line to the already-open newbie tip, -- gated on canAddRestStateLine. EXHAUST_TOOLTIP4 (time to fully rested) needs -- GetTimeToWellRested, which is nil on this wire — the line simply never renders, -- faithfully (the binding's note). function BenillaExhaustionToolTipText() if SHOW_NEWBIE_TIPS ~= "1" then local x, y = BenillaExhaustionTick:GetCenter() if BenillaExhaustionTick:IsVisible() then if x >= (GetScreenWidth() / 2) then GameTooltip:SetOwner(BenillaExhaustionTick, "ANCHOR_LEFT") else GameTooltip:SetOwner(BenillaExhaustionTick, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") end else GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, UIParent) end end local exhaustionStateID, exhaustionStateName, exhaustionStateMultiplier = GetRestState() local exhaustionThreshold = GetXPExhaustion() exhaustionStateMultiplier = exhaustionStateMultiplier * 100 local exhaustionCountdown = nil if GetTimeToWellRested() then exhaustionCountdown = GetTimeToWellRested() / 60 end local tooltipText = format(EXHAUST_TOOLTIP1, exhaustionStateName, exhaustionStateMultiplier) local append = nil if IsResting() then if exhaustionThreshold and exhaustionCountdown then append = format(EXHAUST_TOOLTIP4, exhaustionCountdown) end elseif exhaustionStateID == 4 or exhaustionStateID == 5 then append = EXHAUST_TOOLTIP2 end if append then tooltipText = tooltipText .. append end if SHOW_NEWBIE_TIPS ~= "1" then GameTooltip:SetText(tooltipText) else if GameTooltip.canAddRestStateLine then GameTooltip:AddLine("\n" .. tooltipText) GameTooltip:Show() GameTooltip.canAddRestStateLine = nil end end end
-- Driven from the XP BAR's OnUpdate (the ref wires it there, not on the tick — the timer -- only ever counts while the mouse is on the bar, which is what arms it). function BenillaExhaustionTick_OnUpdate(elapsed) if BenillaExhaustionTick.timer then if BenillaExhaustionTick.timer < 0 then BenillaExhaustionToolTipText() BenillaExhaustionTick.timer = nil else BenillaExhaustionTick.timer = BenillaExhaustionTick.timer - elapsed end end end
-- ref-MainMenuBar.xml l.104-110 (the overlay child's OnLoad): the numerals wiring lives -- in the OVERLAY frame's own OnLoad because there its FontString is guaranteed -- materialized; the bar's lockShow starts at the not-hovered refcount. function BenillaExpBarOverlay_OnLoad() if SetTextStatusBarText then -- engine tests load file subsets BenillaExpBar.lockShow = 0 SetTextStatusBarText(BenillaExpBar, BenillaExpBarText) end end
-- ── The performance ("ping") meter ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- ref-MainMenuBar.xml l.344-407: a 16x64 frame in the bar's own right-hand recess whose -- 20x66 bar texture is TINTED green/yellow/red by the connection's latency, plus an -- all-points button on top for the hover tooltip. The thresholds, the 10 s poll and the -- inline handlers below are the ref's, transcribed out of its XML into named functions. -- The meter shows LATENCY ONLY: 1.12 never scales the bar's height, only its color. PERFORMANCEBAR_LOW_LATENCY = 300 PERFORMANCEBAR_MEDIUM_LATENCY = 600 PERFORMANCEBAR_UPDATE_INTERVAL = 10
-- ref-GlobalStrings.lua l.2659 / l.2689 / l.2746 (enUS), fallback form — see the XP bar's -- note above for why these never override a real localized install. MAINMENUBAR_LATENCY_LABEL = MAINMENUBAR_LATENCY_LABEL or "Latency:" MILLISECONDS_ABBR = MILLISECONDS_ABBR or "ms" NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_LATENCY = NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_LATENCY or "The average time it takes to talk with the game server. A low latency will display as a green bar, higher latencies will be yellow or even red. Consistently high latencies may indicate a problem with your Internet connection."
function BenillaPerformanceBar_OnLoad(frame) frame.hover = nil -- 0, not the interval: the ref's first OnUpdate tick runs the poll immediately, so the -- bar is never briefly untinted (its texture is grey until the first SetVertexColor). frame.updateInterval = 0 end
function BenillaPerformanceBar_TooltipText() local _, _, latency = GetNetStats() return MAINMENUBAR_LATENCY_LABEL .. " " .. latency .. MILLISECONDS_ABBR end
-- ref l.389 (the held-open refresh) and l.400 (OnEnter), both the same call: -- GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip(MAINMENUBAR_LATENCY_LABEL.." "..latency..MILLISECONDS_ABBR, -- 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_LATENCY) -- So the reference hover is TWO lines — the number, then the wrapped explanation — seated -- at the default screen corner, not beside the meter (GameTooltip.xml, decision 0661). function BenillaPerformanceBar_ShowTooltip(owner) if not GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip then return end -- engine tests load file subsets GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip(owner, BenillaPerformanceBar_TooltipText(), 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_LATENCY) end
function BenillaPerformanceBar_OnUpdate(frame, elapsed) if frame.updateInterval > 0 then frame.updateInterval = frame.updateInterval - elapsed return end frame.updateInterval = PERFORMANCEBAR_UPDATE_INTERVAL local _, _, latency = GetNetStats() if latency > PERFORMANCEBAR_MEDIUM_LATENCY then BenillaPerformanceBar:SetVertexColor(1, 0, 0) elseif latency > PERFORMANCEBAR_LOW_LATENCY then BenillaPerformanceBar:SetVertexColor(1, 1, 0) else BenillaPerformanceBar:SetVertexColor(0, 1, 0) end -- Held-open tooltips re-read the number on the same 10 s beat (the ref's own refresh). if frame.hover then BenillaPerformanceBar_ShowTooltip(frame) end end
function BenillaPerformanceBar_OnEnter(button) BenillaPerformanceBarFrame.hover = 1 BenillaPerformanceBar_ShowTooltip(button) end
function BenillaPerformanceBar_OnLeave() BenillaPerformanceBarFrame.hover = nil if GameTooltip then GameTooltip:Hide() end end

Scripts.OnValueChanged: if this:IsShown() and TextStatusBar_OnValueChanged then TextStatusBar_OnValueChanged() end
